C. Withheld Recon:ls If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part on any claimed
basis, you must provide a written privilege log identifying: (a) the specific record or category
of records withheld; (b) the specific legal basis for withholding; (c) a description sufficient to

General or conclusory assertions of privilege are insufficient.
D. " Communications" means every manner or means of disclosure, transfer, or exchange of
information, whether oral, written, electronic, or by any other means.
E. "Relating to" means concerning, referring to, describing, evidencing, constituting, or being
in any way legally, logically, or factually connected with the matter discussed.
F. "Relevant Period" means January 1, 2003, through the present, inclusive, except for those
documents pertaining to Number 9 listed above, for which the time period is unlimited.
G. ''You" and "Your'' refers to the United States Attorney's Office, District of New Mexico,
its current and former employees, agents, representatives, and any persons acting on its behalf ..
H. Continuing Obligation This subpoena imposes a continuing obligation to supplement your
production promptly upon discovering additional responsive records.
V. NOTICE OF PRESERVATION OBLIGATION
Upon receipt of this Subpoena, you and all officers, employees, agents, and contractors of the United
States Attorney's Office, District of New Mexico are hereby formally notified that you must
immediately preserve and protect from destruction, alteration, deletion, or loss any and all records
potentially responsive to this Subpoena. This preservation obligation extends to all paper documents,
ESI, backup tapes, email archives, text messages, instant messages, and any other recorded
information, whether stored on United States Attorney's Office, District of New Mexico systems,
personal devices, or third-party platforms.
The destruction, concealment, or material alteration of records subject to a legislative subpoena may
constitute obstruction of a legislative proceeding and may expose responsible individuals and entities
to criminal and civil liability under applicable New Mexico law, including but not limited to NMSA
1978, § 14-3-18 (unlawful destruction of public records) and the New Mexico Governmental Conduct
Act, NMSA 1978, §§ 10-16-1 et seq. The Commission further reserves the right to seek preliminary
injunctive relief under Rule 1-066 NMRA prohibiting the destruction, alteration, or concealment of
any records subject to this Subpoena if there is reason to believe responsive records are at risk
